topic: Governing AI with trust as a deliverable
angle: Trust must be operationalized in AI programs with measurable controls, not mission statements.
sourceTitle: Governing AI with intention in the social impact sector
linkedinPost:
In mission-driven work, trust isn’t marketing. It’s the product.

McKinsey’s piece on governing AI in the social impact sector captures a lesson every enterprise should internalize: adoption without trust is a boomerang. It comes back as complaints, churn, or regulatory heat.

From the front lines, “governance” only works when it shows up as controls people can see and measure. Here’s what I see working: a living use-case registry with a simple risk tier; consent and data provenance surfaced to the end user; human appeal paths defined by SLA; and audit trails that don’t require a hero to reconstruct.

Make trust a KPI: track percentage of AI decisions with explainer views, opt-out rates, and resolution time on escalations. Put a community advisory group or customer council in the loop before launch, not after headlines.

Your model may be state-of-the-art. Your process needs to be state-of-reassurance.

If you had to ship one new “trust control” this quarter, what would your customers actually notice? #AITransformation #EnterpriseAI #CustomerExperience #AIStrategy
xPost: AI governance that works is visible. Ship controls users notice: clear consent, explainer views, human appeal SLAs, and audit trails. Make trust a KPI, not a poster. #AITransformation #EnterpriseAI
